title: Deciding Whether to Say Something About a Friend's Withdrawal
script: Ayu: [concerned] Bram, have you noticed how withdrawn Dimas has become since the divorce was finalized? He's turned down every invitation for nearly two months now.
Bram: [thoughtful] I have, actually. Part of me assumed he just needed space, but two months is starting to feel less like space and more like avoidance.
Ayu: [hesitant] That's exactly what worries me. I don't want to intrude on something that's genuinely none of my business, but I also don't want to mistake respect for neglect.
Bram: [considering] There's a difference between giving someone room to grieve and letting them disappear because confronting it feels awkward.
Ayu: [honestly] I keep telling myself he'll reach out when he's ready, except people who are struggling the most are often the least likely to ask for help.
Bram: [curious] So what would you actually say to him, if you did reach out?
Ayu: [thoughtful] Nothing dramatic. I wouldn't mention the divorce unless he brought it up himself; I'd just say I missed him and ask if he wanted company, no agenda attached.
Bram: [agreeing] That seems wiser than a direct question about how he's coping, which might make him feel like he's being examined rather than simply visited.
Ayu: [determined] Should we go together, or would that feel more like an intervention than a friend dropping by casually?
Bram: [considering] Better if it's just one of us at first. Two people showing up unannounced might come across as alarming rather than comforting.
Ayu: [warmly] I'll go, then, since we've always been closer, and I'll let you know honestly how he seems, whether or not he wants to talk further.
Bram: [thoughtful] Fair enough. And if he does open up, don't rush him toward advice; sometimes being listened to matters far more than being fixed.
Ayu: [reflective] You're right. I've been more anxious about saying the wrong thing than about actually being present, which isn't much better than staying away entirely.
Bram: [encouraging] Just showing up will likely mean more than whatever you end up saying anyway.
Ayu: [determined] Alright. I'll stop by this weekend, and hopefully this is just a rough patch rather than something he's slowly sinking into.
Bram: [warmly] Whatever happens, at least he'll know someone noticed, instead of assuming nobody did.

quiz.question: Why is Ayu concerned about Dimas?
options: He moved away suddenly
He has turned down every invitation for nearly two months since his divorce
He stopped answering phone calls only
He got a new job
quiz.explanation: Ayu says Dimas has turned down every invitation for nearly two months since the divorce was finalized.

quiz.question: What distinction does Bram draw about giving someone space?
options: Space and avoidance are always the same thing
There's a difference between giving room to grieve and letting someone disappear out of awkwardness
Space never helps anyone
Only family should give someone space
quiz.explanation: Bram distinguishes between giving someone room to grieve and quietly letting them disappear because confronting the situation feels awkward.

quiz.question: What does Ayu plan to say to Dimas if she visits?
options: Ask him directly how he is coping with the divorce
Say she missed him and ask if he wants company, without an agenda
Tell him he needs to see a therapist
Avoid mentioning anything personal at all
quiz.explanation: Ayu says she'd just say she missed him and ask if he wanted company, no agenda attached, unless he brings up the divorce himself.

quiz.question: Why do they decide only one of them should visit at first?
options: Bram is too busy to go
Two people arriving unannounced might feel alarming rather than comforting
Dimas only likes Ayu
It saves them time
quiz.explanation: Bram suggests that two people showing up unannounced might come across as more alarming than comforting.

quiz.question: What advice does Bram give if Dimas does open up?
options: Give him a long list of solutions immediately
Don't rush him toward advice, since being listened to matters more than being fixed
Change the subject quickly
Tell him to move on from the divorce
quiz.explanation: Bram advises not rushing Dimas toward advice, since being listened to matters far more than being fixed.
